The Pac-12 Health Analytics Program/CARE-Affiliated Program is a conference-specific registry, not U.S. High School RIO, the NCAA Injury Surveillance Program, or national U.S. surveillance. The paper explicitly contrasts its Pac-12 athlete-year analysis with prior NCAA athlete-exposure studies. Only the clean women's soccer subgroup is extracted. Methods and all Results, Tables 1-2, the contact-level Figure, Discussion, limitations, and references were scanned. Table 1 directly reports 182 soccer concussions overall and 34/36/39/17/40/16 by academic season; Table 2 directly reports the matching overall and annual incidences per 100 athlete-years with 95% CIs. No soccer athlete-year total was printed, so exposure was not back-calculated from count/rate; the printed 14,486 athlete-years and 815 unique athletes are all-sport totals and were not copied. Soccer had more than 5 represented teams, but the exact number and soccer-specific player count/age were not reported. The contact-class figure is pooled across sports and was not mapped. Soccer-specific illness, severity, recurrence, mechanism, location, burden, match/training, and time-loss metrics were absent; the authors state that mechanism was not directly assessed.

The paper directly reports 20 non-contact time-loss injury cases, no repeat injuries, and a study-specific usable injury rate of 4.5 per 1000 h, but not raw total exposure; no exposure was calculated. The reported overall rate is therefore retained on the first row only. The four source muscle-group percentages (hamstring 35%, quadriceps 25%, adductors 25%, gastrocnemius 15%) use the stable 20-injury numerator: permitted percentage-to-count mapping gives thigh 17 and lower leg 3, and their transparent sum gives 20 muscle injuries. Figures and Tables 1-3 concern ACWR prediction/model performance and add no other schema-compatible injury outcome values. The selected injured/non-injured case-control framing and small sample warrant reviewer attention.

notes.body:
Manual source extraction, GPT-5 high-reasoning review. Tables 1-3 and Figures 1, 2, 4 scanned. All-season plus exact season rows retained. Exposure is not directly reported and is blank; rates were not back-calculated. Figure 2 rates are not text-label exact enough for extraction.

Source: Tables 1-3, Figures 1, 2, 4, pp. 4-7.

Table 3 enrichment (2026-07-12): pooled six-season injury-type data added. Direct mean days out mapped to exact schema rows where one-to-one: contusion 8.5 (n=62), tendinosis 48.9 (n=49), ligament sprain/dislocation 25.73 (n=57), fracture 63.6 (n=12), meniscus/cartilage lesion 109.4 (n=11), bursitis 11.8 (n=4), tendon rupture 63.7 (n=3), concussion 9.5 (n=2), abrasion 13 (n=1), laceration 1 (n=1). Table 3 non-contact counts summed directly across injury types = 210 (8+57+45+32+31+21+5+6+3+2+0+0+0), stored as pooled injuryNonContact. Table 3 does not report days-out or non-contact values by season; season-aligned cells remain blank (no back-calculation). Muscle cramps (DOMS), muscle rupture, and other bone injury were not forced into mixed/broader schema rows for severity because no one-to-one field exists. Source: Table 3, p. 6.

Derived exposure note: football match exposure was derived from the official London 2012 tournament schedule using 58 total matches (32 men's + 26 women's) x 11 players x 1.5 hours x 2 teams = 1914 player-hours. This study examines concussive injuries in collegiate recreational athletes across club and intramural sports at a single US university, not a football-specific epidemiology cohort. It identified 135 concussions among 1,088 documented injuries; intramural concussion incidence was 0.57 per 1000 athletic exposures, and the highest intramural AE rate was in outdoor soccer at 0.99 per 1000 AE.

Clarification after review: multi-sport alone is not the exclusion reason here. This paper was archived because it studies collegiate recreational club and intramural sports at a single US university, which is not an inclusion-eligible competitive football cohort. Soccer appears only within that broader recreational program; the paper identifies 135 concussions among 1088 documented injuries, with the highest intramural AE rate in outdoor soccer at 0.99 per 1000 AE.
